# BenchCAD census and reach curve

Generated by `uv run arris-gym census --corpus benchcad --out DIR` from
`BenchCAD/BenchCAD`, `code_gen`, revision
`5919f578ab09ec283603a082fab07c7639ab56eb`. No source programs are committed.
The 17,900 programs all parse. The aggregate census digest remains C1's
`043db6d912c7b77e4b0bc570b9160b2153286279f11a69ceccc57a63193d13ee`.

`programs.jsonl.gz` holds canonical JSON lines sorted by stem, with each
program's SHA-256, family, census outcome and corpus source, revision and
licence. Gzip has `mtime=0`. `reach.json` starts at 1,871/17,900 and admits
one missing census item (form, selector or end form) per step, greedily by
programs immediately unlocked, then by programs still missing it, then kind
and key. Seven forms reach 4,523/17,900 (25.27%); the first selector, `>Z`,
is the fifteenth item; twenty-four reach 9,061/17,900 (50.62%) and all 57
reach 17,900. Zero-gain items remain. `manifest.json` records the uncompressed rows' SHA-256 and the
validated census and reach digests. Two independent census runs give equal
bytes and digests.

These counts and stems are adapted from [BenchCAD](https://huggingface.co/datasets/BenchCAD/BenchCAD)
and shared under its [CC-BY-4.0 licence](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/).


## The table

`fidelity.json.gz` is the `FidelityTable` of all 17,900 programs under `cq` (arris
0.10.0) against the oracle (CadQuery 2.3.0,
`cadquery-ocp` 7.9.3.0), with C1's verdicts (`tests/fixtures/c1/verdicts.json`:
the 100 `lobed_knob` rows `arris_bug`) and its own (`verdicts.json`, below); `oracle.jsonl.gz` the oracle's rows
(STEP text and wall-clock time left out); `arris-report.json` / `.md` the arris
report; `reach-report.json` the `ReachReport` under today's `cq` subset. Written by
`uv run --extra corpus tools/cq_corpus.py --corpus benchcad --verdicts
tests/fixtures/c1/verdicts.json tests/fixtures/c2/benchcad/verdicts.json
--oracle-rows tests/fixtures/c2/benchcad/oracle.jsonl.gz --chunk 100` (network, the
oracle environment; outside the gate), which saves its work in chunks and resumes.
No program text is committed. Each figure is over all 17,900 programs. Re-run by
plans/lift-edges-and-blends step 8 (2026-11-15), after `Workplane.edges`, `fillet` and `chamfer`, the selectors `|X |Y |Z` and `'>Z or <Z'`, the seams a blend passes over and `faces`'s finer estimate beside a thin curved face were lifted (ADR-0020, ADR-0017's amendment of 2026-11-15); before that, by
plans/lift-arrays-and-blind-cuts step 7 (2026-11-15), after `Workplane.rarray`, `polarArray` and `cutBlind` and the contexts they open were lifted; before that, by

**The oracle rows are the baseline's bytes**, and not the re-run's. The re-run's
oracle gave the same status, solids and faces for every program, but 214 rows
of 8 families (`sheet_metal_tray` 101, `washer` 49, `spacer_ring` 32,
`snap_clip` 13, `ratchet_sector` 11, `hollow_tube` 3, `spline_hub` 3,
`parallel_key` 2) differed from the baseline in their report only: the STEP's
SHA-256 and the last digits of centroid, volume and area (at most 4e-13
relative). The same program on the same code returns the baseline's bytes on
some runs and not on others: Open CASCADE's boolean, chamfer and shell order
depends on memory addresses (address-space layout and a job's position on its
zygote). No fidelity row moved (all 214 are the same as the baseline's, so the
table's digest does not depend on which oracle bytes are kept), so the baseline
rows stay committed (BACKLOG Findings `oracle-nondeterministic-step`).

The one before it (plans/lift-sphere step 5, reach 4,011, 2,734 agree, no in-subset `cq_bug`) had digest `651fe2c161d62d738f67632f2c01a4ccd590ea73fa2634665206ae9a373c1f5a`.

## The 717's diagnosis

`cq-bugs.json` archives a rerun of the baseline's 717 statically in-subset
`cq_bug` programs, from `uv run --extra corpus tools/cq_diagnose.py`.
The tool does not import or run the oracle. Every selected row retains its
stem, family, program SHA-256, status, message verbatim, versions, source and
CC-BY-4.0 licence; no program text or wall-clock value is stored. The
histogram counts every row, and names its families:

- `cq.Workplane('YZ')`: 319 programs.
- `cq.Workplane('XZ')`: 285 programs.
- `Workplane.circle on a non-empty stack`: 113 programs, all `torus_link`.

The constructor's string form admits plane values the implementation refuses;
the circles are drawn after `moveTo` puts a point on the stack. These are first
failures; later calls have not yet run. Shrunk strict-xfail regressions live in
`regression/cq-plane-yz`, `regression/cq-plane-xz` and
`regression/cq-circle-at-point`. No declaration is removed, so diagnosing the
failures does not change reach or the baseline table's digest above.

Two independent diagnosis runs give identical JSON bytes. The archive pins the
baseline table's digest (above); it remains that baseline's diagnosis now the
table is regenerated after the fixes: all 717 are in the subset and none is a
`cq_bug` row (604 agree, 70 `torus_link` agree, 43 `arris_refusal`). Attribution and licence are the
same BenchCAD CC-BY-4.0 attribution linked above.

## Verdicts

`verdicts.json` holds the verdicts of the rows no rule classes (ADR-0006), by stem: C1's 100 `lobed_knob` verdicts are in `tests/fixtures/c1/verdicts.json` and are not repeated. Written by `uv run --extra corpus tools/cq_closed_forms.py --table tests/fixtures/c2/benchcad/fidelity.json.gz --oracle-rows tests/fixtures/c2/benchcad/oracle.jsonl.gz --out tests/fixtures/c2/benchcad/verdicts.json --refusal cotter_pin=tests/fixtures/regression/cq-tangent-cylinders --arris-bug shaft_collar=tests/fixtures/regression/cq-cross-hole-bounds --arris-bug clevis_pin=tests/fixtures/regression/cq-cross-hole-bounds --arris-bug spacer_ring_008375_s20260505=tests/fixtures/regression/cq-chamfer-slot-bounds --arris-bug shaft_collar_016155_s20260505=tests/fixtures/regression/cq-chamfers-overlap-on-a-face` (plans/lift-cylinder step 5, plans/lift-face-selectors step 7c, plans/lift-holes-and-points step 7a, plans/lift-arrays-and-blind-cuts steps 6a and 6b, plans/lift-edges-and-blends steps 7c and 7d; a `--refusal` or `--arris-bug` takes a family or, winning over it, one stem; a row a family's `--arris-bug` would class is classed only if `check_bug_cause` finds its fixture's cause in it, else it stays unclassified, counted and named on stderr, and a row with a closed form of its own takes that), from the repository's root on the committed table (a row a verdict classes is read as one no rule classes; a row arris ended `unsupported_api` gets none), which checks each verdict with `compare` against both sides before writing it: 841 `occt_wrong` rows by their closed forms, where arris is within the ADR-0005 constants of the closed form and Open CASCADE is not: 64 `t_pipe_fitting` tees and 77 flanged ones with a `polarArray` of bolt holes (step 6a), 25 `bellows` (a revolved profile, holes cut blind through the flange and the rim, step 6b), 202 `u_bolt` and 184 `j_hook` half-torus hooks (the last 125 of them with the nut's prism under the box, plans/lift-extrude-both step 4), 17 `manifold_block` (bores crossing bores, the counterbores on the block's edge) and 15 `connecting_rod` (a cross hole into a ring's wall) by `part_measures` (fluxes through the boundary, each face's patch exact interval arithmetic along lines on it, plans/lift-holes-and-points step 7a), and the rows the edges and blends newly run: 82 `sprocket` and 126 `double_simplex_sprocket` (Open CASCADE's chamfer of the tooth outline takes less than the mitre, `sprocket_measures`, step 7b and 7d), 29 `pan_head_screw`, 16 chamfered `manifold_block` (a closed form with the chamfer's planes) and 1 more `connecting_rod`, 2 slotted `spacer_ring` (`slotted_ring_closed_form`, step 7c) and `shaft_collar_004924` (`collar_measures`: a chamfered collar with a tunnel cut through each wall, its three cuts one cylinder, Open CASCADE 3.5e-7 off in volume; step 7c's repair); 159 `cotter_pin` rows `arris_refusal` by `regression/cq-tangent-cylinders`; and 152 rows `arris_bug`: 151 `ok` on both sides with arris's box loose, which `check_bounds_cause` holds each row to (24 `shaft_collar` and 126 `clevis_pin` by `regression/cq-cross-hole-bounds`, `spacer_ring_008375` by `regression/cq-chamfer-slot-bounds`), and `shaft_collar_016155` (arris's `OpInternalError`, the oracle `invalid`) by `regression/cq-chamfers-overlap-on-a-face`. The file holds 1,152 verdicts. Re-run on the committed table, it writes the committed file byte for byte. The table is run with `--verdicts tests/fixtures/c1/verdicts.json tests/fixtures/c2/benchcad/verdicts.json`.
